(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 04.11.2023 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Bidar, in MVC No.371/2020.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 04.09.2020, the claimant as a pillion rider was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-38/R-7695 from Bidar towards his village Sirsi (A).

One Raju S/o Sambanna was riding the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR said motorcycle and when they reached near the Marzapur cross, on Bidar-Bagdal road, at that time, at 05:45 p.m., the rider rode the motorcycle in a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and due to which, he lost control over his motorcycle and dashed to the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/V-4622 which was coming from the opposite direction.
Due to the accident, the riders and pillion riders of both motorcycles fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the said injuries, the claimant became unconscious and rider of motorcycle bearing Chandrakanth vs Ananda And Anr

on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1161952/
2 Reg.No.KA-38/V-4622 died on the spot.
Immediately, they were shifted to the government hospital Bidar.
Thereafter, the claimant was referred for higher treatment to Kamareddy Ortho and Trauma Care Hospital, Kalaburagi and admitted as inpatient on 05.09.2020 and spent huge amount towards his treatment.

sentences.text: 3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent huge amount towards medical expenses, NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR conveyance charges, etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending motorcycle by its rider.
appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant himself was examined as PW-1 and Dr.S.B.Kamreddy, was examined as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P22.
The respondents did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/R-7695 by its rider, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,29,978/-
along with interest at the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed seeking enhancement.

6. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
i) Firstly, due to the accident, the claimant has suffered the grievous injuries.
He has examined doctor as PW-2.
In his evidence, the doctor has deposed that claimant has suffered 43% disability to the whole body.
The Tribunal has assessed whole body disability at 15% which is on the lower side.

ii) Secondly, she contended that even though the claimant claims that he was doing agricultural labour work and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, the Tribunal has taken the notional income as merely as Rs.10,000/- p.m. which is on the lower side.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR iii)
Lastly, she contended that due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
He was inpatient for a period of 29 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
He has to suffer this trauma throughout his life.
Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
Hence, she sought for allowing the appeal.

3 7.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised following counter contentions:
i.
Firstly, even though doctor has deposed that claimant has suffered 43% disability to the whole body, the doctor has not assessed limb disability.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly considered whole body disability at 15%.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR ii.
Secondly, even though the claimant claims that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, he has not produced any document to establish his income.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed Rs.10,000/- as notional income of the claimant.

iii. Lastly, he contended that considering the evidence of doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, and considering the medical records, the Tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and it does not require any interference.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 04.09.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/R-7695.

Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR i.
10. As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.

PW-2, 
doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered disability of 43% to whole body.
The doctor has not assessed the disability to particular limb.

Therefore,
taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor and injuries mentioned in the w o u n d c e r t i f i c a t e E x . P 4 , d i s c h a r g e s u m m a r y E x . P 7 , w e a r e N C :
2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR of the opinion that whole body disability has to be assessed at 20% instead of 15%.
11.
Even though the claimant claims that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of Chandrakanth vs Ananda And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1161952/
4 proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2020, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.13,750/- p.m.
the claimant was 32 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.

Thus, loss of future earning is reassessed as: Rs.5,28,000/-
(13,750x12x16x20%).
12.
The claimant was inpatient for a period of 29 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment and he has to suffer the same throughout his life.
Considering the evidence of doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering is just and reasonable.
The claimant - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR is entitled for compensation under the head of 'loss of income during laid up period' for three months at Rs.41,250/- (13750x3).
Loss of amenities is to be enhanced from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
13. Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

 Pain and suffering 50,000/- 50,000/-

 Loss of income during 20,000/- 41,250/-
 laid up period

Food and nourishment, 10,000/- 10,000/-
 conveyance and  attendant charges  Loss of future amenities 30,000/- 40,000/-
 Total 9,29,978/- 12,01,228/-
14.

In the result, the following order is passed:
- 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6517-DB HC-KAR ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.

b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.12,01,228/-.

d) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
